cues.say: Component 6: Queue + workers. A to-do list for slow work. The server writes a note and replies at once; background workers pick up notes and do the work. You'll bring this up during version one, when you draw the basic design.
Think of it as: Order tickets on a kitchen rail: the cashier doesn't cook. Use it for emails, texts, image processing, and anything that can lag.
Here's a real scenario. Each paid pizza order sends a confirmation text. The SMS provider takes 1 to 2 seconds and sometimes times out.
Without it: The customer waits on the text before seeing confirmed.
A provider timeout becomes a checkout error.
With it: API queues text order 42 and confirms instantly.
A worker sends the text, retrying on failure.
After 5 failures: dead-letter queue and an alert.
900 orders in 30 minutes: texts lag minutes, none lost.
Why it works: Checkout stays fast, and a slow provider can't break ordering.
In the interview, say: At-least-once delivery, plus workers that are safe to run twice.
A few related terms you may hear.
At-least-once: A note may be handed out twice, so jobs must be safe to repeat.
Dead-letter queue: Where a note goes after N failures. Alert on it.
Queue length: Add workers when the list gets long.
Kafka: A replayable event log for many readers. Overkill here.
Pub/sub: One message delivered to several listeners.
Outbox: Save the message in the same transaction as the order.
